title: 🧠 Processing engines, instruction sets and configurable logic
industry_title: Processors, instruction sets and programmable logic

paras: Processing hardware differs by programmability, data parallelism, latency, energy budget and the work it accelerates—not simply by being a “brain.”

blocks.h2: RISC, CISC, ARM, x86 and RISC-V
paras: An instruction set architecture specifies the software-visible machine interface: instructions, registers, exceptions and memory model. A microarchitecture is the internal implementation (pipelines, caches, predictors, execution units). RISC/CISC are broad historical design traditions, not reliable one-word predictions of energy use or speed.
x86-64 is used by Intel and AMD processors; Arm and RISC-V are distinct ISAs. An ASIC or FPGA can implement RISC or CISC CPU cores; these terms classify different design dimensions.

Source code → compiler/assembler → ISA machine instructions → OS loader → CPU fetch/decode/execute → cache and memory transactions → buses/interconnect → devices. An FPGA design instead uses RTL or higher-level hardware tools → synthesis → place-and-route → configuration bitstream → programmable logic.

Correction to a useful shorthand: an MCU runs firmware, but the firmware is not necessarily “stored in its memory” as a single undifferentiated region; flash, ROM, SRAM and external storage play different roles.
